why: People who depend on the facility: more people within reach means more patients per system. The 0-1,500 people/km2 range drops urban cells (EAE's top density class). Towns are on the grid (1,102 on-grid facilities sit in denser cells, only 26 unelectrified ones), and without the filter Kampala ranks 2nd with no unelectrified facility at all.
Poverty proxy. In the Assistance Need Index poorer areas score higher: facilities there cannot rely on user fees, so they depend on public money.
The programme is about facilities, so this layer carries the most weight. The 0-5 km range keeps the analysis to areas within Uganda's 5 km access standard for a health facility.

Grid proximity. In the Assistance Need Index, areas farther from the 11/33 kV network score higher because utilities are less likely to reach them. No >2 km filter: most unelectrified facilities sit next to a line (Section 2), so a filter would drop them.
